speaker: Unknown
en: So Ben, if you can believe it, how long it's been since we last did this.
zh: 那么 Ben,如果你能相信的话,距离我们上次做这个已经过去多久了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The world was very different, no AI at the time.
zh: 当时世界非常不同,还没有 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked about aggregation theory mostly.
zh: 我们主要谈论的是聚合理论。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought a fun place to begin, since the world has changed so much, is to hear what you think it would mean for the US to win the AI race.
zh: 我认为一个有趣的开场,既然世界已经发生了如此大的变化,就是听听你认为美国赢得 AI 竞赛意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it would be very problematic for the US to win.
zh: 我认为美国获胜会是非常有问题的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say we take the most sort of fantastical scenario where if you control AI, you basically, your military is better than anyone else.
zh: 假设我们取最奇幻的情景:如果你控制了 AI,基本上你的军队就比任何人都强。

speaker: Unknown
en: Somehow it fixes their manufacturing, all these things that I don't think AI is necessarily going to do because they sort of deal with the real world.
zh: 不知怎么它还修复了制造业,以及所有这些我不认为 AI 一定会做到的事情,因为这些问题某种程度上要应对现实世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in this world, what is the game theory optimal response of China?
zh: 但在这个世界里,中国的博弈论最优回应是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: To blow up TSMC.
zh: 炸掉 TSMC。

speaker: Unknown
en: Game theory can get very sort of convoluted and complex.
zh: 博弈论可以变得非常曲折复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, this one actually isn't that complicated.
zh: 对我来说,这个其实没那么复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a fundamental disconnect that I have with a lot of the rhetoric coming out of Silicon Valley, coming out, I think, of one of the labs in particular, where if we get to a place where
zh: 我与来自硅谷的很多言论——我认为尤其是来自其中一家实验室的言论——存在一个根本性的脱节,如果我们到达一个地方,

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a meaningful superiority in terms of a military, national security perspective.
zh: 我们在军事、国家安全视角方面拥有显著的优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's very dangerous for the world.
zh: 我认为那对世界来说是非常危险的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in that state, how much does it extend beyond TSMC being blown up?
zh: 但在这种状态下,这会延伸到 TSMC 被炸掉之外多少呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because in that state, I would assume we figured out how to build fabs here in the US, you know, to some degree and are less reliant on that one choke point.
zh: 因为在这种状态下,我会假设我们在某种程度上已经想清楚了如何在美国本土建厂,从而不那么依赖那一个咽喉点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a little bit of magical thinking which I just invoked in terms of manufacturing and whether it be fabs, whether that be actuators, all these precursors.
zh: 我认为这里有一点我刚刚提到的关于制造业的魔幻思维,无论是晶圆厂,还是执行器,所有这些前置要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the degree to which we are dependent on China is underappreciated and is not something that is going to be fixed outside of a conflict.
zh: 我认为我们对中国的依赖程度被低估了,而且这不是在冲突之外能够解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just because fixing so many of these things is going to be
zh: 仅仅因为修复这么多这些东西将会是

speaker: Unknown
en: Dramatically dumb.
zh: 极其愚蠢的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If your competitor is sourcing from China and you're going to start sourcing or getting things from the U.S., you're going to be at such a disadvantage, relatively speaking, that you're just not going to do it.
zh: 如果你的竞争对手从中国采购,而你要开始从美国采购或获取东西,你将处于如此大的相对劣势,以至于你根本不会去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you do it when you have literally no choice.
zh: 所以你只会在真的别无选择时才去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that works for very big headline items.
zh: 而这适用于非常重大的头条项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can browbeat Apple to move some of their iPhone manufacturing to India, for example.
zh: 例如,你可以逼迫 Apple 把他们的一部分 iPhone 制造转移到印度。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even that is a good example because Apple is not truly moving out of China.
zh: 但即便那也是一个好例子,因为 Apple 并没有真正迁出中国。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're diversifying to an extent.
zh: 他们在一定程度上是在分散化。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would just cost so much.
zh: 那成本会高得吓人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like paying an insurance policy that if you don't have to pay it and it's astronomically expensive, you're just not going to pay it.
zh: 就像买一份保险，如果没必要付，而且价格贵得离谱，你根本不会去付。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one of those sort of hypotheses that I just have a hard time even grokking because the only world I see where we truly
zh: 这属于那种我甚至很难理解的一类假设，因为我能看到的唯一一个世界里，我们真正

speaker: Unknown
en: Pull out and have no dependency on China such that if they want to blow up Taiwan, who cares?
zh: 撤出并对中国毫无依赖——这样如果他们想炸掉台湾，谁在乎呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no impact on us.
zh: 对我们没有任何影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems pretty fantastical to me.
zh: 在我看来这相当荒诞离奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's a bit of facing reality in this regard that is not present in these conversations.
zh: 而且我认为在这方面需要一点直面现实的态度，而这些对话中恰恰缺少这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Put yourself in their shoes.
zh: 换位思考一下，站在他们的角度。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think the motivations are?
zh: 你认为他们的动机是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone
zh: 每个人

speaker: Unknown
en: Can use a good bogeyman.
zh: 都可以用得上一个好用的假想敌。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think from the AI trade perspective, nothing works better than we have to beat China.
zh: 我认为从 AI 交易的角度来看，没有什么比“我们必须打败中国”更管用的了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I do think we need to beat China.
zh: 而我也确实认为我们需要打败中国。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to be competitive.
zh: 我们需要保持竞争力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I despair at the extent to which over the last few years in particular, so many of our responses, particularly from a political perspective, has been to try to be like China.
zh: 让我感到绝望的是，尤其是过去几年，我们的很多应对方式，特别是从政治角度来说，一直是试图变得像中国一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we should be going the other direction, more openness, more innovation, less top-down control, less restrictions on
zh: 我认为我们应该走相反的方向：更开放、更多创新、更少的自上而下的控制、更少的对

speaker: Unknown
en: speech and things along those lines.
zh: 言论之类事情的 restrictions(限制)。

speaker: Unknown
en: America succeeds by being on the leading edge and by leading into that.
zh: 美国的成功靠的是站在最前沿，并朝着那个方向引领。

speaker: Unknown
en: You said probably the U.S. being purely dominant in AI is not the right end state for the world.
zh: 你说过，美国在 AI 上纯粹占主导地位可能不是对世界而言的正确终局状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is your ideal equilibrium for how this goes worldwide?
zh: 那么你理想中的全球局面(均衡)是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a bit where AI right now is kind of like the Taiwan situation in that the current status quo actually doesn't seem so bad.
zh: 有一点是，现在的 AI 有点像台湾问题，就是当前的现状实际上看起来并没有那么糟。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question is, how sustainable is it?
zh: 问题是，它的可持续性如何？

speaker: Unknown
en: But maybe it's sustainable for longer than we think.
zh: 但也许它的可持续时间比我们想象的要长。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way I think about it right now is I think OpenAI and Anthropic are clearly on the frontier.
zh: 我现在思考它的方式是，我认为 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 显然处于前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who knows what's happening with Google and then Grok and Meta are chasing them.
zh: 谁知道 Google 那边在发生什么，然后 Grok 和 Meta 在追赶他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Meanwhile, the Chinese are very capable, very smart, and also definitely distilling these models to sort of stay about six to nine months behind.
zh: 与此同时，中国人非常有能力、非常聪明，而且也确实在蒸馏这些模型，以保持落后大约六到九个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels like a pretty good equilibrium that I think is generally favorable to the U.S.
zh: 这感觉是一个相当不错的均衡，而且我认为总体上对美国有利。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the question is, how long can it stay this way?
zh: 现在，问题是，这种局面能维持多久？

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's lots of questions on there, like, can the Chinese actually pull ahead?
zh: 这上面有很多问题，比如，中国人真的能反超吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm still a little skeptical for various reasons, whether it be from chips.
zh: 基于种种原因，我还是有点怀疑，比如芯片方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Getting to the leading edge in that last six to nine months is very difficult.
zh: 要在最后那六到九个月里达到最前沿是非常困难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be instructive how Meta and Grok do in terms of actually catching up.
zh: Meta 和 Grok 在实际追赶方面表现得如何，将会很有启示意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: Especially as we get to the world of AI improving itself, using AI to make the AI better, which I think is definitely a real thing.
zh: 尤其是当我们进入 AI 自我改进的世界，用 AI 让 AI 变得更好——我认为这确实是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you see a real acceleration from both OpenAI and Anthropic recently, which was sort of theorized and it seems to be coming true.
zh: 我认为你最近能从 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 身上看到真正的加速，这此前只是理论上的，而现在似乎正在成为现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to the extent that's true, can you actually catch up?
zh: 而如果这是真的，你真的能追上吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the other question about this, by the way, is to what extent does that apply to cost to serve, to marginal costs?
zh: 顺便说一句，我认为关于这个的另一个问题是，这在多大程度上适用于服务成本、边际成本？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can apply AI to optimizing your stack, to figuring things out, to analyzing all the data,
zh: 如果你能把 AI 应用于优化你的技术栈、解决各种问题、分析所有数据，

speaker: Unknown
en: Is your cost to serve structurally lower than anyone else?
zh: 你的服务成本会不会在结构上低于其他任何人？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the thing about the open source models.
zh: 这就是开源模型的问题所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: The talk about them being free is bizarre to me because it's marginal costs.
zh: 说什么它们是免费的，我觉得很奇怪，因为那是边际成本的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You still have to run inference like GLM or Kimi.
zh: 你还是得跑推理，比如 GLM 或 Kimi。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kimi is very expensive to serve.
zh: Kimi 的服务成本非常昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: The cost per answer is significantly higher.
zh: 每次回答的成本明显更高。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone referring to these as free, it feels like in the narrative, it's in people's head that...
zh: 每个人把这些说成是免费的，在叙事里，人们脑子里似乎觉得……

speaker: Unknown
en: Free is free.
zh: 免费就是免费。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I can use AI for free.
zh: 现在我可以免费使用 AI 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, you can't use AI for free.
zh: 不，你不能免费使用 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not paying necessarily the R&D to create the AI, but you're definitely paying the inference to sort of run it.
zh: 你不一定支付了创造 AI 的研发费用，但你肯定在支付运行它的推理成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: So right now I kind of like where we are and the pushback would be that's right now.
zh: 所以现在我还挺喜欢我们所处的位置，而反对意见会是：那只是现在。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not going to stay that way, which I think is fair pushback, but I don't know this way longer than we think.
zh: 不会一直这样，我认为这是合理的反对意见，但我不知道这种局面会不会比我们想的持续更久。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you could know anything about the future of how this will go to be more confident in like where the equilibrium will end up, what is it?
zh: 如果你能预先知道这件事将如何发展的未来的任何情况，从而对均衡最终会落在哪里更有信心，那会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it like the length of the S-curve?
zh: 就占 GDP 的百分比而言，它不是最后一次更大的建设浪潮，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like how far up the S-curve we are?
zh: 还是像我们处于 S 曲线上多高的位置？

speaker: Unknown
en: At some point, these things presumably will level out, maybe not.
zh: 在某个时间点，这些东西大概会趋于平缓，也许不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would be the thing you'd want to know that would give you a better sense of what the future might look like?
zh: 你想要知道的、能让你更好感知未来可能是什么样的事情会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I am concerned that with the scare around people freaking out about Mythos and this Hugging Face incident, that the actual implication of that is not that we reduce these dangers, but we just stop releasing stuff.
zh: 我担心的是，围绕人们对 Mythos 感到恐慌以及这起 Hugging Face 事件的恐慌，其实际影响不是我们减少了这些危险，而是我们只是不再发布东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We on the outside start to lose any sense of like where exactly what is actually the frontier and where it is.
zh: 我们外部的人开始失去对前沿究竟是什么、它究竟在哪里的任何感知。

speaker: Unknown
en: There becomes sort of a false sense of security because right now everyone's basing their understanding of Mythos on Fable, but how good is Fable actually relative to Mythos?
zh: 会出现某种虚假的安全感，因为现在每个人都是基于 Fable 来理解 Mythos 的，但 Fable 相对于 Mythos 到底有多好？

speaker: Unknown
en: That sort of gap is only going to, I think, increase over time.
zh: 我认为这种差距只会随着时间推移而扩大。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that's a real question that I'm not sure about.
zh: 所以我认为这是一个我不确定的真实问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: This question of the recursiveness and AI sort of making itself better, does that lead to some sort of takeoff?
zh: 这个递归性的问题、AI 某种程度上让自身变得更好，这是否会导致某种起飞？

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the end of the day, there's
zh: 而归根结底，还有

speaker: Unknown
en: Timing questions in lots of different ways.
zh: 以多种不同方式呈现的时机问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm worried about the timing mismatch in terms of the actual return on investment producing enough revenue to fuel investment.
zh: 我担心的是时机错配，即实际的投资回报能否产生足够的收入来支撑投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're working our way down the capital curve.
zh: 我们正在沿着资本曲线往下走。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started with free cash flow.
zh: 我们从自由现金流开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: The speed with which the tech companies blew through the debt markets is kind of incredible.
zh: 科技公司穿透债务市场的速度简直令人难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took like a year.
zh: 大概只花了一年时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now Google is issuing equity.
zh: 然后现在 Google 在发行股票。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA is putting together these $500 billion
zh: NVIDIA 正在拼凑这些 5000 亿美元的

speaker: Unknown
en: This fire and billy dollar thing to tap into like pension funds and insurance floats and things like that.
zh: 这个 fire and billy dollar 的东西，去撬动养老金基金和保险浮存金之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's after that?
zh: 那之后是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where's the money come after that?
zh: 那之后钱从哪里来？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, ideally, we actually flip back to free cash flow funding this.
zh: 嗯，理想情况下，我们实际上会翻转回由自由现金流来为这一切提供资金。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if there's a gap there, if we don't get there soon enough, then...
zh: 但如果那里存在缺口，如果我们没能足够快地到达那一步，那么……

speaker: Unknown
en: We could have a big blow up.
zh: 我们可能会有一场大崩盘。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that you're ready when the next cycle comes around, which requires a ton of guts and a ton of discipline and a ton of money.

en: I think the memory solution will be solved eventually.

zh: TSMC 可以说更糟，因为只有一家。

en: It's the same thing.

zh: 所有市场都带有风险。

en: And a lot of the question is, who ends up holding the risk?
zh: 而很多问题在于，最终是谁承担着风险？

en: What I think a lot of the tech companies didn't fully appreciate is the extent to which TSMC has offloaded risk onto the big tech companies.
zh: 我认为很多科技公司没有完全意识到的是，TSMC 在多大程度上把风险转嫁给了大型科技公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the way they've done that is the risk that TSMC is worried about is overcapacity.
zh: 而他们做到这一点的方式是：TSMC 所担心的风险是产能过剩。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we build too much, it's not just that we built too much and we have all these fixed costs that are not being fully utilized.
zh: 如果我们建得太多，不只是我们建多了、有很多没有被充分利用的固定成本的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if we build a fab, we expect that fab to run for 30 years.
zh: 但如果我们建一座晶圆厂，我们期望这座厂能运行 30 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've like baked in too much capacity into the system for years and years and years.
zh: 相当于我们把过多的产能固化进了系统里，一年又一年又一年。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they are very biased towards being much more conservative.
zh: 所以他们非常倾向于更加保守。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a little bit of a culture component to this, too.
zh: 这里面也有一点文化因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the most interesting TSMC stories, it's kind of analogous, that Samsung story, was Morris Chang retired in like the late 2000s.
zh: 最有意思的台积电故事之一，和那个三星故事有点类似，是张忠谋大约在 2000 年代末退休了。

speaker: Unknown
en: New leadership took over.
zh: no—[[556]] 新领导层接任。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was the Great Recession.
zh: 然后爆发了大衰退。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they pulled back their planned spending.
zh: 于是他们缩减了计划中的支出。

speaker: Unknown
en: He comes in, fires everyone.
zh: 他回来了，把所有人炒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's like, the iPhone just launched.
zh: 他说，iPhone 刚刚发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the biggest opportunity we've ever seen.
zh: 这是我们见过的最大的机遇。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to be investing, not cutting.
zh: 我们需要投资，而不是削减。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they invested through the Great Recession and through that downturn.
zh: 于是他们在大衰退期间、在那次下行周期中持续投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what laid the foundation for them taking over sort of weeding edge semiconductors in that time.
zh: 这正是奠定了他们那个时期接管最尖端半导体的基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: Morse Chang is a one of one.
zh: 张忠谋是独一无二的。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the Mount Rushmore, in my mind, of the greatest and most impactful tech executives of all time, the entire fabulous model is so critical to what tech is and what it does, and also just the guts to do that at that time, particularly in someone who lived there, a culture that doesn't necessarily tend to make those sorts of bets.
zh: 在我心中，他位列史上最伟大、最有影响力的科技高管的“总统山”之上，整个晶圆厂模式对科技是什么、科技做什么至关重要，而且还有在当时敢那么做的胆识，尤其他是一个生活在那里的人，那个文化未必倾向于做那种赌注。

speaker: Unknown
en: TSMC, they were pretty conservative, to be totally honest.
zh: 台积电，说实话，他们相当保守。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what happens though?
zh: 那么结果怎样呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where'd the risk go?
zh: 风险去哪儿了？

speaker: Unknown
en: TSMC's like, we don't want to take the risk.
zh: 台积电说，我们不想承担风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: Risk doesn't disappear.
zh: 风险不会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just moves.
zh: 它只是移动了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The risk is right now where you have every single big tech company realizes if we had more compute, we could be making more money.
zh: 现在的风险在于，每一家大型科技公司都意识到，如果我们有更多算力，我们就能赚更多的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's lots of foregone revenue and foregone profits that is the manifestation of the risk that TSMC handed off to them.
zh: 所以有大量错失的营收和错失的利润，这就是台积电转嫁给他们的风险的体现。

speaker: Unknown
en: Risk doesn't disappear.
zh: 风险不会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just gets handed off.
zh: 它只是被转手了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes that risk doesn't manifest in losing money.
zh: 有时这种风险不是以亏钱的形式显现。

speaker: Unknown
en: It manifests in not making money.
zh: 而是以没赚到钱的形式显现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there is money not being made right now because what happened was they were very excited about 5G.
zh: 而现在确实有钱没赚到，因为当时的情况是，他们对 5G 非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: They did a big wave of like investment, expanding their fabs in around 2020, 2021, 22.
zh: 他们大约在 2020、2021、22 年做了一波大规模投资，扩建他们的晶圆厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're like, oh, yeah, we're good.
zh: 然后他们说，哦，好啊，我们没问题了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I said, 2024, ChatGPT comes out in 2022.
zh: 就像我说的，2024 年，而 ChatGPT 在 2022 年发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: Big thing in tech in 2023.
zh: 2023 年科技界的大事。

speaker: Unknown
en: In 2024, their growth rate went down.
zh: 2024 年，他们的增长率下降了。

speaker: Unknown
en: In 2025, their growth rate went down.
zh: 2025 年，他们的增长率又下降了。

speaker: Unknown
en: In 2026, it's up now.
zh: 2026 年，现在回升了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very funny because I was writing about this a while ago, and then I think it was like one or two earnings calls ago.
zh: 非常有趣，因为我前段时间在写这个，然后我想是在一两次财报电话会之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Suddenly...
zh: 突然……

speaker: Unknown
en: CeCe Wei, the CEO and chairman, is talking about, like, use cases for AI, the whole earnings call in a way he never had before.
zh: 魏哲家，CEO 兼董事长，在整个财报电话会上前所未有地大谈 AI 的用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is why the merrymakers are scared.
zh: 这就是造市者们害怕的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Usually there's like a bullwhip and they're worried about being at the end of the bullwhip where the demand happens and it works its way down the chain and they're at the end and then they double down.
zh: 通常会有牛鞭效应，他们担心自己处在牛鞭的末端，需求发生在前端，然后沿着链条传导下来，而他们在末端，然后他们加倍投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's already too late.
zh: 但已经太晚了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're wasting all their money.
zh: 他们浪费了所有的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the thing with AI is...
zh: 而 AI 这件事在于……

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's a bullwhip, it's like the longest bullwhip of all time.
zh: 如果这是牛鞭效应，那它就像是有史以来最长的牛鞭。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's still so much to be built.
zh: 还有那么多东西要建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it just took a while for Asia to get the message where these sort of companies are.
zh: 只是亚洲这边过了好一阵子才收到消息，就是这些公司所在的亚洲。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they've by and large gotten it, but them getting the message, it then takes several years for that to actually materialize.
zh: 我想他们大体上已经收到了，但从收到消息到真正落地实现，还需要好几年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have a sense for how long you think it will take given the extreme shortage of compute?
zh: 鉴于算力的极度短缺，你觉得还需要多长时间，你有感觉吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The interesting thing is what this means for Intel and Samsung's sort of logic business.
zh: 有意思的是这对 Intel 和三星的逻辑业务意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been writing about the problem of this dependency on TSMC for years.
zh: 多年来我一直在写关于这种对 TSMC 依赖的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my first articles in 2013 was exhorting Intel.
zh: 我 2013 年最早的文章之一就是在敦促 Intel。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I say you have to build a fab business.
zh: 嗯，我说你必须建一个晶圆厂业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not going to be a designer anymore.
zh: 你不能再只做设计商了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a huge business in manufacturing chips.
zh: 制造芯片有巨大的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought I was late writing it then.
zh: 我当时觉得自己写这个已经晚了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their stock goes to the moon throughout the 2010s as they're riding the sort of cloud wave.
zh: 整个 2010 年代他们的股票一路涨上天，因为他们搭上了云计算的浪潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it wasn't until 2020 where they finally realize we fell behind.
zh: 直到 2020 年他们才终于意识到，我们落后了。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, there's this huge opportunity.
zh: 顺便说一句，这里有一个巨大的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're totally unprepared for it.
zh: 我们完全没有准备好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have a customer service mindset or culture organization or all the IP building blocks and all these things that TSMC has.
zh: 我们没有客户服务的心态或文化、组织，也没有 TSMC 拥有的所有 IP 积木和所有这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they need a customer.
zh: 而且他们需要一个客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: They need customers to help them actually
zh: 他们需要客户来帮助他们真正

speaker: Unknown
en: Build a real foundry business.
zh: 建立一个真正的代工业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would write about this as a problem.
zh: 所以我会把这作为一个问题来写。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I write about the China issue.
zh: 我也写中国问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you're dependent on a company that is 60 miles offshore of our greatest geopolitical opponent who thinks it's theirs.
zh: 比如你依赖一家公司，它离我们最大的地缘政治对手只有 60 英里的海域，而那个对手认为台湾是它的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these are big problems.
zh: 所以这些都是大问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's where I came to appreciate this insurance issue.
zh: 这就是我开始理解这个保险问题的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a big tech company to go to Intel and say, Intel, you make our chip.
zh: 一家大型科技公司跑到 Intel 面前说，Intel，你来造我们的芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, the biggest benefactor of this is going to be you, because you're going to learn how to work with a partner.
zh: 顺便说一句，这件事最大的受益者将是你，因为你会学到如何与合作伙伴共事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the biggest
zh: 而最大的

speaker: Unknown
en: Paint is going to be us because we're going to have to figure out how to work with you.
zh: 痛苦将属于我们，因为我们得摸索出怎么跟你合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could just go to TSMC.
zh: 我们本来可以直接去找 TSMC。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are awesome.
zh: 他们非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are so great to work with.
zh: 跟他们合作太舒服了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We know they're going to do a good job.
zh: 我们知道他们会把活干好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just never made rational sense for anyone to go work with Intel.
zh: 从理性上讲，去找 Intel 合作对任何人来说从来都不划算。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was their fundamental problem.
zh: 那就是他们的根本问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: In an unchanging world, TSMC would just win forever.
zh: 在一个不变的世界里，TSMC 会永远赢下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is where TSMC, in some respects, made the same mistake as the money makers, made the same mistakes as I ran, if I can continue the analogy.
zh: 但正是在这一点上，TSMC 在某些方面犯了和那些赚钱机器一样的错误，如果我可以继续这个类比的话，也犯了和伊朗一样的错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they didn't invest the last few years, the shortages are going to be so acute.
zh: 因为他们过去几年没有投资，短缺将会非常严重。

speaker: Unknown
en: Big 10 companies that were foregoing so much revenue and so many profits because we don't have enough compute.
zh: 那些前十大公司因为算力不足而放弃了那么多收入和那么多利润。

speaker: Unknown
en: We will go through the pain of getting Intel up to speed, of getting Samsung's logic up to speed.
zh: 我们愿意承受把 Intel 拉到合格水平、把三星逻辑业务拉到合格水平的痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: The scarcity is what ultimately save Intel.
zh: 稀缺最终拯救了 Intel。

speaker: Unknown
en: I expect at some point that they're going to announce some major partner for the first time.
zh: 我预计在某个时候，他们会首次宣布某个重要的合作伙伴。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be a big deal.
zh: 那将是一件大事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But ultimately, TSMC brought it on themselves.
zh: 但归根结底，这是 TSMC 自己招来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the cure for high prices is high prices thing.
zh: 这就是「治愈高价的药方是高价」那个道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to route around them.
zh: 我们会绕开他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's all these things as like an analyst sitting on the side.
zh: 作为一个坐在旁边的分析师，有这么多这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can write these things.
zh: 你可以把这些东西写出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's one of those things I sort of learned.
zh: 这也是我 somewhat 学到的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one's going to pay insurance that they don't need to pay when that insurance expected value is negative.
zh: 当那份保险的期望值为负时，没有人会去支付他们不必支付的保险。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way to solve the geopolitical problem of dependence on TSMC is to come up with a compute use case that is so massive that everyone is economically incentivized to bring other people up to speed.
zh: 解决依赖 TSMC 这一地缘政治问题的方法，是想出一个如此庞大的算力用例，以至于每个人在经济上都有动力去帮助其他人达到合格水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we get the sort of...
zh: 然后我们就得到了那种……

speaker: Unknown
en: Geopolitical Insurance for free.
zh: 免费的地缘政治保险。

en: If you think about the, let's say, top 10 or 15 technology companies, which ones do you think have the most interesting setups today for their business?
zh: 如果你想想，比方说，排名前 10 或 15 的科技公司，你认为今天哪些公司的业务布局最有意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer is always Amazon.
zh: 答案永远是 Amazon。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason Amazon is so compelling is the extent to which they build for them.
zh: Amazon 之所以如此有吸引力，就在于他们在多大程度上为自己的需求而构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are their first best customer.
zh: 他们是自己的第一个也是最好的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: They provide the scale to get basically anything off the ground, which they then sell to other people.
zh: 他们提供了把几乎任何东西做起来的规模，然后再把它卖给其他人。

speaker: Unknown
en: AWS is the most obvious example.
zh: AWS 是最明显的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: AWS, contrary to sort of popular thought, was not spare Amazon capacity.
zh: 与流行的看法相反，AWS 并不是 Amazon 的闲置产能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, it took a long time to get Amazon.com onto AWS.
zh: 实际上，把 Amazon.com 迁移到 AWS 上花了很长时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: What it drove was the understanding that we can't be having so many meetings.
zh: 它带来的是这样一种认识：我们不能开这么多会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we need to have just compute that you can plug in purely API surface.
zh: 比如说，我们需要的是纯 API 界面就能即插即用的算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't need to talk to anyone.
zh: 你不需要跟任何人谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just there.
zh: 它就在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And oh, by the way, if we do that for our internal retail teams, we could do that for anyone.
zh: 顺便说一句，如果我们能为内部零售团队做到这一点，我们就能为任何人做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turns out the retail is so big, we have to start with everyone else.
zh: 结果发现零售业务太大了，我们必须先从其他所有人开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: AWS actually started serving external customers before it served internal ones, but now it serves them all.
zh: AWS 实际上在服务内部客户之前就开始服务外部客户了，但现在是两者都服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got other products like say the logistics, where it was the opposite.
zh: 还有其他产品，比如说物流，情况正好相反。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right now we're using external providers for logistics, UPS and FedEx and USPS.
zh: 现在我们在物流上用的是外部供应商，UPS、FedEx 和 USPS。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to build this up ourselves.
zh: 我们需要自己把它建起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now they built it up themselves.
zh: 然后他们真的自己建起来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're offering to third parties.
zh: 正因为他们是 Graviton 的第一个也是最好的客户，Graviton 变得更好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Other people can use their delivery services.
zh: 其他人可以使用他们的配送服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: You see this in market after market.
zh: 你在一个又一个市场里都能看到这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're talking about some of their AI products or their chip products.
zh: 他们在谈论自己的一些 AI 产品或芯片产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the beauty of the Graviton or the Trainium, particularly the early versions?
zh: Graviton 或 Trainium 的美妙之处是什么，尤其是早期版本？

speaker: Unknown
en: The early versions were terrible.
zh: 早期版本非常糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you're on Amazon and you're using some of their managed services, like, say, the Redshift database service, they don't tell you what the processor is underneath that.
zh: 但如果你在 Amazon 上使用他们的一些托管服务，比如说 Redshift 数据库服务，他们不会告诉你底层用的是什么处理器。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're just buying a managed service.
zh: 你只是在购买一项托管服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they can put all their crappy processors underneath the services they're selling, and that gives them the volume and the capacity to iterate them and get better.
zh: 所以他们可以把所有那些糟糕的处理器塞进他们所卖的服务底下，这给了他们迭代改进的产量和容量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they get to the point where they can actually sell them externally.
zh: 然后他们就能达到真正可以向外出售的地步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they were the first best customer for Graviton, Graviton got better.
zh: 因为他们是 Graviton 的第一个最佳客户,Graviton 变得更好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they were the first best customer for Tranium, Tranium got better.
zh: 正因为他们是 Trainium 的第一个也是最好的客户，Trainium 变得更好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now Tranium is obviously running Anthropic and AI products.
zh: 而现在 Trainium 显然在支撑着 Anthropic 和 AI 产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll see if any of them take off.
zh: 我们拭目看这些有没有哪个能成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have call center software.
zh: 他们有呼叫中心软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their call center...
zh: 他们的呼叫中心……

speaker: Unknown
en: Or their customer experience is going through AI.
zh: 或者说他们的客户体验正在经历 AI 化。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, it's pretty good.
zh: 顺便说一下，效果还挺不错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I haven't tried it.
zh: 我没试过。

en: Moving back to America, I've been buying lots of stuff.
zh: 说回美国，我最近买了很多东西。

en: Every summer I'd buy lots of stuff in a very brief amount of time.

en: Meta doesn't talk about that.
zh: Meta 不谈论这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mark Zuckerberg has never really talked about the societal benefits of advertising, except in passing, in 20 years.
zh: 在这 20 年里,Mark Zuckerberg 从来没有真正谈论过广告的社会效益,最多只是顺带一提。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's handed it off to other people to take care of it, and maybe there's a bit where him not paying attention is why there is a certain grit and grind that goes into building an advertising business.
zh: 他把它交给了其他人去处理,也许在某种程度上,正是他不予关注,才导致建立广告业务时存在某种摩擦和艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: People get frustrated or have questions about it as far as data and all those sorts of things.
zh: 人们在数据之类的问题上会感到沮丧或产生疑问。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe there was a bit where he didn't want to be involved in it and wipe his hands of it.
zh: 也许在某种程度上,他不想参与其中,想撇清关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you saw this when Apple passed ATT, app tracking transparency was
zh: 但当 Apple 通过 ATT——应用追踪透明度——时,你看到了这一点,

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the worst antitrust violations in the history of technology, Apple unilaterally obliterating all these business models while they're simultaneously building their own as far as advertising goes and doing all this tracking.
zh: 那是科技史上最严重的反垄断违规行为之一,Apple 单方面摧毁了所有这些商业模式,而与此同时他们自己却在广告方面建立自己的业务,并做着所有这些追踪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why?
zh: 为什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Trust us.
zh: 相信我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And meanwhile, they're running these advertisements.
zh: 与此同时,他们自己在投放这些广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember that advertisement of people on the bus, like overhearing everyone around them, what they're saying.
zh: 我记得那个广告,公交车上的人仿佛能听到周围每个人在说什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was such a dishonest representation of how advertising works on the internet.
zh: 那是对互联网广告运作方式的极不诚实的描绘。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had Tim Cook in Congress talking about companies selling data.
zh: 你有 Tim Cook 在国会谈论公司出售数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Facebook's not selling your data.
zh: Facebook 并不出售你的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's value to them.
zh: 数据对他们来说就是价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would they sell the data?
zh: 他们为什么要出售数据呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Meta was not prepared to respond.
zh: Meta 没有准备好做出回应。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you got this to Sheryl Sandberg back in the day.
zh: 我想这得从当年说起,是 Sheryl Sandberg 的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: She, in every call, would talk about advertising, how great it is and have a bunch of case studies, people who are benefiting from advertising and these new entrepreneurs.
zh: 她在每一次财报电话会上都会谈论广告,谈它有多好,并有一堆案例研究,讲那些从广告中受益的人,还有这些新创业者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then she left and it's kind of like that hole never got filled.
zh: 然后她离开了,那种空缺似乎就再也没被填补。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like it's a company that's kind of like embarrassed.
zh: 感觉这像是一家有点难为情的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We make a lot of money from ads, but we got glasses and we're doing AI.
zh: 我们从广告赚很多钱,但我们有了眼镜,我们在做 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like you have ads and ads are awesome.
zh: 可是你有广告,而广告很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if they had communicated that more consistently, they would be in a better place generally from a PR perspective.
zh: 我认为如果他们更一致地传达这一点,他们在整体上、从公关的角度来看,会处于更好的境地。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would have been in a better place relative to Apple.
zh: 它们相对于 Apple 会处于更好的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think they would have an easier time right now convincing Wall Street that let us invest.
zh: 而且我认为它们现在要说服华尔街让我们投资会更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other problem is they've spent cumulative hundred some billion dollars on Oculus, which I dated all along.
zh: 另一个问题是,它们在 Oculus 上累计花了大概一千多亿美元,而我从一开始就不看好这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a bit where, why should we let you spend money again?
zh: 所以就有一点在于,凭什么再让你花钱?

speaker: Unknown
en: The one major player and company that we haven't talked about much is Jensen and NVIDIA.
zh: 我们还没怎么聊过的一个主要玩家和公司是 Jensen 和 NVIDIA。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm curious how you would tie this back to the notion of not understanding commodity markets in Silicon Valley, whether or not you think compute ultimately is a commodity.
zh: 我很好奇你会怎么把这联系回「不理解硅谷的大宗商品市场」这个说法,以及你是否认为算力最终会变成大宗商品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious whether or not you think intelligence will ultimately be a commodity.
zh: 我也很好奇你是否认为智能最终会变成大宗商品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's interesting that intelligence and compute, which seem to be by far the most interesting and important topics in tech, both might be commodities and less differentiated than taxpayer products.
zh: 有意思的是,智能和算力——它们显然是目前科技领域最有意思也最重要的两个话题——最终可能都是大宗商品,差异化程度甚至比纳税人的产品还低。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, that's always the case, though.
zh: 不过,事情一直就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: The most interesting thing about the internet is free distribution.
zh: 互联网最有意思的地方就是免费分发。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bandwidth is a commodity.
zh: 带宽是大宗商品。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fact that I can pull out my phone right now and connect to any information source in the world for free, free on a marginal cost basis, is because it's a commodity.
zh: 我现在能掏出手机,免费连上世界上任何信息源——按边际成本算是免费的——正是因为它是个大宗商品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It changed the world.
zh: 它改变了世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Commodities change the world.
zh: 大宗商品改变世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a aspect of differentiated products by definition have lower TAMs because there's an elasticity aspect to it.
zh: 有一点是,差异化产品按定义 TAM 更小,因为存在弹性因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not everyone can afford to pay for it.
zh: 不是每个人都付得起。

speaker: Unknown
en: People's willingness to pay is going to differ.
zh: 人们的支付意愿是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your market is going to be constrained.
zh: 你的市场会因此受限。

speaker: Unknown
en: Apple's never going to serve the whole world by selling a device, whereas a Google can because it's free.
zh: Apple 靠卖设备永远不可能服务全世界,而 Google 可以,因为它是免费的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That matters.
zh: 这很关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're paying for a commodity, but to the extent it is available to everyone is the extent it is impactful.
zh: 你在为一种大宗商品付费,但它能触及每个人的程度,就是它产生影响的程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: The internet is a commodity.
zh: 互联网是大宗商品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It changed the world.
zh: 它改变了世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't think it'd be weird that intelligence ends up a commodity and changes the world.
zh: 所以我不认为智能最终变成大宗商品并改变世界有什么奇怪的。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of these often are not thought of as as good of businesses as these differentiated high margin products.
zh: 这类东西往往不被认为是像那些差异化高利润产品一样好的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Curious for your thoughts on Jensen and NVIDIA specifically.
zh: 很想听听你对 Jensen 和 NVIDIA 具体怎么看。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA's position is, I think, definitely unnatural.
zh: 我认为 NVIDIA 的地位绝对是不自然的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You look at NVIDIA, they've maintained all their margins.
zh: 你看 NVIDIA,它们一直维持着全部利润率。

speaker: Unknown
en: Isn't that amazing?
zh: 这是不是很惊人?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's 2026 and everyone's coming for them and they're still charging.
zh: 都 2026 年了,所有人都在抢它们的生意,它们还在收那么多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: However much money for a chip, but they're actually not maintaining their margins because this whole question of circular financing is people talk about Lucent and things like that.
zh: 一颗芯片收那么多钱,但其实它们并没有维持住利润率,因为循环融资这个整体问题——人们会谈到 Lucent 之类的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, this whole deal and NVIDIA is providing a 25% backstop.
zh: 而且,你知道,这整笔交易,NVIDIA 提供了 25% 的兜底担保。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you actually ascribe a value to that, to NVIDIA's
zh: 但如果你真的给这个赋予一个价值——NVIDIA

speaker: Unknown
en: Taking equity in the neoclouds or whatever, they guarantee they're gonna buy all their compute to 2030.
zh: 持有这些新云(neocloud)的股权之类的,它们担保对方到 2030 年会买下它们所有的算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do they do that?
zh: 它们为什么要这么做?

speaker: Unknown
en: So that the entity in question can get a lower cost of capital, so they can buy more GPUs, et cetera.
zh: 这样做是为了让这个主体能获得更低的资本成本,从而能买更多 GPU,等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But implicit in that, why do they get a lower cost of capital?
zh: 但隐含在其中的是,它们为什么能获得更低的资本成本?

speaker: Unknown
en: They get a lower cost of capital because NVIDIA assumed risk.
zh: 它们能获得更低的资本成本,是因为 NVIDIA 承担了风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is my point before, risk never disappears, it just appears somewhere else.
zh: 这就是我之前说的观点:风险不会消失,只会转移到别的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Taking on risk has a price.
zh: 承担风险是有代价的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a world where AI takes off, it never stops, and everything is fine, and NVIDIA captured all the upside of their risk.
zh: 存在一种世界:AI 起飞,永不停止,一切顺利,NVIDIA 把自己承担的风险的上行收益全部收入囊中。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's also a world where...
zh: 但也存在另一种世界……

speaker: Unknown
en: Say that this is Neocloud they backed up.
zh: 比如说这是它们兜底的那家新云。

speaker: Unknown
en: A ton of compute comes to market.
zh: 大量算力涌入市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: The hyperscalers have plenty of compute.
zh: 超大规模云厂商有足够多的算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't have enough compute.
zh: 它们算力不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA is paying for a compute that no one wants.
zh: NVIDIA 在为没人要的算力买单。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just lost a bunch of money.
zh: 它们刚刚亏了一大笔钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about it, there's an expected value of that investment.
zh: 如果你这样想,这笔投资有一个期望值。

speaker: Unknown
en: That expected value, it's not zero.
zh: 那个期望值,并不是零。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not 100%.

speaker: Unknown
en: It's somewhere in the middle.
zh: 而是在中间某处。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that is a diminution of NVIDIA's profitability.
zh: 但这是对 NVIDIA 盈利能力的一种削减。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you actually look at their business holistically,
zh: 如果你真正从整体上看他们的业务，

speaker: Unknown
en: What that is, is a price cut.
zh: 那实际上是什么？就是一次降价。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the price cut didn't show up in margins, it didn't show up in what they're offering, but a lot of what NVIDIA is doing is how can we maintain our margins even if the wide view, sort of discounted cash flow, expected value, holistic view of our company.
zh: 现在，这次降价没有体现在利润率上，也没有体现在他们提供的东西上，但 NVIDIA 做的很多事都是：即使从宽泛的视角、折现现金流、期望值、整体的公司视角来看，我们如何维持我们的利润率。

speaker: Unknown
en: People do discount cash flows, but are you actually considering all these pieces?
zh: 人们确实会做现金流折现，但你真的把这些因素都考虑进去了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The reality is, is that moving stuff off the balance sheet by and large works.
zh: 现实是，把东西从资产负债表上挪出去，总体上是有效的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they're doing all these deals to maintain what feels somewhat unnatural.
zh: 但他们做所有这些交易，是为了维持一种感觉上有点不自然的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have seen price cuts.
zh: 我们确实看到了降价。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're just manifesting in these very bizarre sort of ways.
zh: 它们只是以这些非常怪异的方式显现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, in the long run, I think the challenge is their ultimate competitors are the hyperscalers, particularly Google and Amazon.
zh: 现在，从长远来看，我认为挑战在于他们最终的竞争对手是超大规模云厂商，尤其是 Google 和 Amazon。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Google and Amazon aren't just building their own chips, but they're also looking to sell those chips externally.
zh: 所以 Google 和 Amazon 不只是在造自己的芯片，它们还打算把这些芯片对外销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google already made a deal to sell like 20% of their TPUs to Anthropic.
zh: Google 已经达成协议，要把大约 20% 的 TPU 卖给 Anthropic。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the last earnings call, Andy Jassy practically confirmed that they'll be selling Trinium 3s, or maybe Trinium 4s, or they'll be selling Trinium chips sort of eventually externally, which makes sense.
zh: 在最近一次财报电话会议上，Andy Jassy 几乎确认了他们最终会对外销售 Trinium 3，或者可能是 Trinium 4，或者说他们会对外销售 Trinium 芯片，这是合理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That gives them a long-term buy-in to these companies.
zh: 这让这些公司产生了长期的买入承诺。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a huge amount of R&D that goes into developing chips.
zh: 开发芯片需要大量的研发投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: They get more leverage on their spend.
zh: 这样他们能在支出上获得更多杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: It all makes sense.
zh: 这一切都说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, they're not selling their chips on differentiation.
zh: 顺便说一句，他们卖芯片靠的不是差异化。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're selling their chips as commodities.
zh: 他们是把芯片当作大宗商品来卖的。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA is the one selling differentiation.
zh: 卖差异化的才是 NVIDIA。

speaker: Unknown
en: People aren't going to Amazon to use Tranium.
zh: 人们去 Amazon 不是为了用 Tranium。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they're not cannibalizing the attractiveness of their cloud by selling Tranium outside.
zh: 所以他们把 Tranium 卖到外面，并不会蚕食自己云的吸引力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they're NVIDIA's biggest problem because what's the number one advantage that the hyperscalers have?
zh: 所以他们是 NVIDIA 最大的问题，因为超大规模云厂商的第一大优势是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Lower cost of capital.
zh: 更低的资本成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a capital fight.
zh: 这是一场资本之争。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have a lower cost of capital than the NeoClouds do.
zh: 他们的资本成本比 NeoCloud 低。

speaker: Unknown
en: The NeoClouds are, they'll buy NVIDIA left, right, and center.
zh: NeoCloud 呢，他们会到处大量买 NVIDIA。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, it also makes total sense that why SpaceX, like Elon's out there, we will always buy NVIDIA because they're the best.
zh: 顺便说一句，这也完全解释了为什么 SpaceX——比如 Elon 在外面说的——我们会永远买 NVIDIA，因为他们是最好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, you'll buy NVIDIA because they're the most fungible.
zh: 不，你买 NVIDIA 是因为他们最通用、最容易变现。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA is true.
zh: NVIDIA 是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is the most fungible.
zh: 它确实是最通用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: CUDA's moat is dramatically diminished because the models don't care what they run on, and that's what actually matters, what's built on top of the models.
zh: CUDA 的护城河已经大幅减弱，因为模型并不在乎自己跑在什么上面，而真正重要的是构建在模型之上的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it still matters.
zh: 但它仍然有影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still something of a moat.
zh: 它仍然算是一种护城河。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to play the game SpaceX is doing, where we're going to build a lot and rent it out, but reserve the right to pull it back, of course you're going to be on NVIDIA because the easiest way to rent it out is to be on NVIDIA.
zh: 如果你想玩 SpaceX 正在玩的那种游戏——我们要建很多然后租出去，但保留收回来的权利——你当然会用 NVIDIA，因为租出去最简单的方式就是用 NVIDIA。

speaker: Unknown
en: You saw this very early, by the way.
zh: 顺便说一句，你很早就看到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: You go back to 2024, 2023, NVIDIA starts talking about all these sovereign clouds.
zh: 回到 2024 年、2023 年，NVIDIA 开始谈论这些主权云。

speaker: Unknown
en: They start talking about, they tried to get all these Neotron models.
zh: 他们开始谈论，他们试图推出所有这些 Neotron 模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: They had this thing in 2024, I remember, it was the first one where it was like the rockstar GTC at San Jose and like the huge Coliseum and just no one comes out.
zh: 我记得 2024 年有一场，那是第一次在圣何塞办那种摇滚明星式的 GTC，有巨大的圆形剧场，结果几乎没人来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a very boring GTC.
zh: 那是一场非常无聊的 GTC。

speaker: Unknown
en: The old ones used to be NVIDIA demonstrating like 50 gazillion things as they're throwing stuff at the wall.
zh: 以前的 GTC 是 NVIDIA 演示数不清的东西，什么都往墙上扔。

speaker: Unknown
en: They knew they had something with GPUs and they're trying to like...
zh: 他们知道自己手里有 GPU 这个好东西，然后试图……

speaker: Unknown
en: Get people excited about them, yeah.
zh: 让人们为之兴奋，对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once LM showed up, it's like, oh, we have the use case.
zh: 一旦 LM 出现，就像是，哦，我们有应用场景了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they were coming up with all these enterprise offerings.
zh: 但在那之前他们搞出了一堆企业级产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't remember what they were called.
zh: 我记不清叫什么了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like these modules, basically, that, of course, they were free, but they only ran on NVIDIA.
zh: 基本上就是这些模块，当然，它们是免费的，但只能在 NVIDIA 上运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you could see what they were doing is they were trying to lock people in.
zh: 而你可以看出他们在做的，就是试图把人们锁定进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Intel is a good example here.
zh: Intel 是这里的一个好例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: AMD cleaned them out in hyperscaler sales.
zh: AMD 在超大规模云厂商的销售中把他们清洗出局了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the hyperscalers were put in the effort to get stuff working on AMD versus Intel.
zh: 因为超大规模云厂商付出了努力让东西在 AMD 上跑通，而不是在 Intel 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are still small differences, even though they're x86.
zh: 即便它们都是 x86,仍然存在一些小的差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they're buying at such scale, the investment to do it is worth it to get a better chip or lower price or whatever it might be.
zh: 因为他们的采购规模如此之大，为获得更好的芯片或更低的价格或其他什么而做的投入是值得的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The part of Intel's business that never floundered was selling to government and selling to enterprises.
zh: Intel 业务中从未衰败的部分是卖给政府和卖给企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't have the resources of a hyperscaler.
zh: 他们没有超大规模云厂商那样的资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not buying at that scale.
zh: 他们不会以那种规模采购。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're just going to keep buying what they had before.
zh: 他们只会继续买以前买的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why NVIDIA talks about selling to sovereign clouds.
zh: 这就是为什么 NVIDIA 谈论向主权云销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why they talk about selling to enterprises because they want to get in these markets where they're not going to be balancing this chip versus that chip.
zh: 这就是为什么他们谈论向企业销售，因为他们想进入这些市场，在那里他们不用去权衡这个芯片还是那个芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: The hyperscalers have always been the threat to NVIDIA for that reason.
zh: 出于这个原因，超大规模云厂商一直是 NVIDIA 的威胁。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're actually bigger.
zh: 他们实际上规模更大。

speaker: Unknown
